candidates.title: BPR-1038: Windows Purge profile admits directories that carry exactly the inherited owner-only entries
criteria: Do you accept this Windows privacy rule for Purge profile: a directory is admitted when it carries either the protected owner-private descriptor, or exactly the owner-private entries inherited from its parent (the user, and the package SID when contained, each with full access, user as owner), and anything else is refused as not private to your account?
candidates.content:
The problem: once the Git isolation existed, Purge profile refused on Windows. The Git owner and Git itself create directories (repositories, objects, refs, packs) with inherited descriptors, and the purge inventory demanded the protected descriptor.

The station chose which side moves: the inventory, under an exact rule. Protecting the Git owner's own directories would still leave the ones Git creates inside them. Only the purge inventory allows the inherited form for a directory; the stores, the catalog and every other caller still require the protected descriptor they write.

Why it is as private: the walk admits each entry only after its parent, from a root that must be protected, and compares the entries themselves. An inherited descriptor that grants anyone else, or grants the owner less, is refused. What it does not pin: a later change to a parent's descriptor would flow down; the parent is itself admitted only in the same exact form, in the same walk.

Existing profiles need no repair. A refusal now reads: "A file or folder in this profile is not private to your account, so nothing was prepared or deleted." application_release_maintenance_public_path passes on Windows; the Windows case refuses one extra Everyone entry; the negative control fails by name; macOS and Linux pass.

The card calls this a security-policy question, so it is put to you although the card is Done. Accept keeps the rule. Reject means it should change; say how in the note.

candidates.title: BPR-0897: may a release build publish to whatever pull request is open?
criteria: Is select_observed_review_mutation composing a live provider for any open pull request the intended behaviour before this product reaches anyone outside this repository? Choose 1, 2 or 3.
candidates.content:
There are two ways to a live review mutation. The attended designated-live lane is gated twice: the pull request's identity is proved field by field before launch, and inside the app nothing is composed unless hostname, owner, name, ids, node ids, OIDs and refs equal compile-time constants. Every piece of live evidence in this tree came through that lane. The other, select_observed_review_mutation, composes the live provider in a non-attended release-configuration build for whatever pull request is open, with the resolve gesture minting its own one-shot grant.

Nothing is known to be wrong; what is missing is a recorded intent. BPR-0641 (enabling normal inline publication for the private alpha) is the same boundary from the other side. One fact bounds the exposure: a reply through the live session cannot currently be submitted at all (BPR-0896); resolve, unresolve and root comments take other paths.

1: yes, as designed; the intent is written next to the composition.
2: yes, but not yet; it gets a gate like the attended lane's until BPR-0641 opens it.
3: only for repositories the person has explicitly designated; that is a product feature.

candidates.title: BPR-0825: where should the one Windows owner-private descriptor definition live?
criteria: Where should the one definition of the Windows owner-private descriptor live, so that a change on the SQLite side cannot silently turn Windows workspace ownership into repair_required: (a), (b) or (c)? Choose one.
candidates.content:
The Git adapter's prepare_workspace_registry requires ApplicationDataRoot to carry exactly the protected descriptor that the SQLite adapter's create_storage_root_owner_private writes (catalog_database.cpp). There are two definitions: the SQLite side's private_security_attributes and validate_private_security, and the agent adapter's header-only windows_private_descriptor and windows_private_to_current_user, which the Git adapter already includes. If they drift, Windows workspace ownership silently reads repair_required.

Found while preparing this item, since the card was parked: 19a3dfd7 (2026-09-20) moved the SQLite side's definition into the header-only src/adapters/native/windows_private_storage.hpp, which the SQLite and logging adapters include by relative path; it is not its own build target or architecture-boundary owner. BPR-1038 (fe7dad99) then changed validate_private_security there, for the purge inventory's directories only. The Git adapter still uses the agent adapter's definition, so the two remain separate.

(a) adds an AdapterGit to AdapterSQLite edge.
(b) adds an AdapterSQLite to AdapterAgent edge.
(c) adds a neutral header-only target that both include, with a new owner entry in the architecture boundaries.

The integrator recommends (c): adapters are narrow host capability ports, and (a) and (b) each add an adapter-to-adapter edge for a platform definition that neither adapter owns. Items 1, 2, 4 and 5 of the card are done on Windows; this is the only open item.
